_comment: Revert / bridge / desk code → bank line (docs/NPCS.md §5). `line` is the main-path apology; `why` is the Ask-why half (protocol words allowed). {release_in} is filled from the record the error names. Keys are the SDK ERROR_SIGNATURES names (@bloxchain/sdk contract-errors), Teller Desk codes, Privy codes and bridge codes.

default.line: Sorry — the counter could not do that.
default.why: The Teller Desk returned an error the branch has no line for yet. The code and message are below.

TargetNotWhitelisted.line: That payee isn't on our approved list.
TargetNotWhitelisted.why: Your account's guard only lets `transfer` be called on targets whitelisted for that selector. The demo token was whitelisted at Account Opening; anything else is refused by the contract.

ResourceNotFound.line: That payee isn't on our approved list — the branch has no record of it.
ResourceNotFound.why: The guard registry has no entry for that target/selector pair. The whitelist is per function selector, not per account.

ItemNotFound.line: The branch has no record of that item.
ItemNotFound.why: A registry lookup (role, function, whitelist entry) found nothing under that key.

ItemAlreadyExists.line: That is already on file — nothing to add.
ItemAlreadyExists.why: The registry refuses a duplicate entry (a role, a selector, a whitelist target). Provisioning treats this as already done.

ResourceAlreadyExists.line: That is already on file — nothing to add.
ResourceAlreadyExists.why: The guard registry already holds this entry.

NoPermission.line: You're not allowed to do that from this counter.
NoPermission.why: The caller does not hold the action required on this selector. Permissions are checked on two selectors — the execution function and the handler — and this caller is missing one of them.

NoPermissionForFunction.line: You're not allowed to do that from this counter.
NoPermissionForFunction.why: The caller has no permission at all for this function selector.

RestrictedOwner.line: Only the account holder can ask for that.
RestrictedOwner.why: This function is restricted to `OWNER_ROLE`. Staff cannot call it for you.

RestrictedOwnerRecovery.line: Only the account holder or Security can ask for that.
RestrictedOwnerRecovery.why: Restricted to the owner or the recovery role.

RestrictedRecovery.line: That is Security's job, not ours.
RestrictedRecovery.why: Restricted to `RECOVERY_ROLE` — the Security Officer at the side door.

RestrictedBroadcaster.line: Only the teller's desk may submit that.
RestrictedBroadcaster.why: Restricted to `BROADCASTER_ROLE`, which the Teller Desk holds.

CannotModifyProtected.line: That part of your file is sealed — it can't be changed here.
CannotModifyProtected.why: Protected roles (owner, broadcaster, recovery) are managed by SecureOwnable, not by the runtime role registry.

BeforeReleaseTime.why: `approveTimeLockExecution` compares the record's `releaseTime` to the block timestamp of the approval and reverts `BeforeReleaseTime` until it has passed. The clock on the wall is that record; Bob's window cannot shorten it. The manager's priority release can bypass it — but only under your own hand-scanned signature, submitted by his role.

TransactionNotPending.line: That wire is no longer waiting in the vault.
TransactionNotPending.why: The record has already been released, recalled or failed — only PENDING records can be approved or cancelled.

CanOnlyApprovePending.line: That wire is no longer waiting in the vault.
CanOnlyApprovePending.why: Approval is only valid for a PENDING record.

CanOnlyCancelPending.line: That wire is no longer waiting in the vault.
CanOnlyCancelPending.why: Cancellation is only valid for a PENDING record.

TransactionNotFound.line: We have no wire by that number.
TransactionNotFound.why: No record with that txId exists on your account.

TransactionStatusMismatch.line: That wire isn't in a state where we can do that.
TransactionStatusMismatch.why: The record's status does not allow this transition.

TransactionIdMismatch.line: The slip and the record don't match — let's write a new one.
TransactionIdMismatch.why: The txId in the signed slip differs from the record it was applied to.

PendingSecureRequest.line: There's already a request of that kind waiting — let it settle first.
PendingSecureRequest.why: SecureOwnable allows one pending request per operation type.

NOT_PENDING.line: That wire is no longer waiting in the vault.
NOT_PENDING.why: The Teller Desk read the record before sending and it was not PENDING any more (released, recalled, or failed).

RECORD_*.line: The vault took the request, but the record didn't end up where we expected — let me check the board.
RECORD_*.why: The transaction was mined but the record's final status was not the one this action should produce. The board is re-read from the chain.

RECORD_FAILED.line: The release was mined, but execution failed — free balance may have been spent down, so nothing was sent.
RECORD_FAILED.why: A release transaction can mine while the AccountBlox record becomes FAILED when the ERC-20 transfer cannot settle, commonly because free balance fell below the requested amount after filing. A pending wire is a count, not escrowed funds; this is an execution failure, not a hand-scan failure.

InvalidSignature.line: That slip isn't signed by the account holder.
InvalidSignature.why: The EIP-712 signature does not recover to `metaTx.params.signer`, or the signer is not the owner.

InvalidSignatureLength.line: That slip isn't signed properly — let's write a new one.
InvalidSignatureLength.why: The signature bytes are not 65 bytes long.

SignerNotAuthorized.line: That slip isn't signed by the account holder.
SignerNotAuthorized.why: The recovered signer does not hold the action the slip claims.

ECDSAInvalidSignature.line: That slip isn't signed properly — let's write a new one.
ECDSAInvalidSignature.why: The signature is malformed (OpenZeppelin ECDSA rejected it).

InvalidSValue.line: That slip isn't signed properly — let's write a new one.
InvalidSValue.why: Malleable or out-of-range `s` component in the signature.

InvalidVValue.line: That slip isn't signed properly — let's write a new one.
InvalidVValue.why: Invalid recovery id `v` in the signature.

MetaTxHandlerSelectorMismatch.line: That slip was written for a different counter.
MetaTxHandlerSelectorMismatch.why: The handler selector in the signed slip does not match the function the broadcaster called (`msg.sig`).

MetaTxHandlerContractMismatch.line: That slip was written for a different branch.
MetaTxHandlerContractMismatch.why: The handler contract in the signed slip is not this account.

InvalidHandlerSelector.line: That slip was written for a different counter.
InvalidHandlerSelector.why: The handler selector is not one this account accepts.

ChainIdMismatch.line: That slip was written for a different wing of the bank.
ChainIdMismatch.why: The chainId in the signed slip is not this chain's. A Remote EVM signature cannot replay elsewhere — by design.

policy_violation.line: The teller's stamp doesn't cover that — the branch can only sign slips for your own account.
policy_violation.why: Privy refused to sign: the request fell outside the per-player policy (verifyingContract / `to` pinned to your account, chainId pinned to this chain). This is the control that stops the session signer touching anyone else's account (K5, V6).

MetaTxExpired.line: That slip expired — let's write a new one.
MetaTxExpired.why: `deadline` is `block.timestamp + duration` at signing time and had passed when the transaction mined. On Remote EVM the block clock is frozen between transactions, so durations are drift-corrected (`metaTxDuration`).

InvalidNonce.line: Someone already used that slip number — writing a fresh one.
InvalidNonce.why: The signer nonce in the slip is not the account's current nonce for that signer. One in-flight slip per player is why the desk serialises them.

GasPriceExceedsMax.line: The network is too expensive for that slip right now.
GasPriceExceedsMax.why: `maxGasPrice` in the slip is below the current gas price.

InsufficientBalance.line: Free balance is lower than the requested amount — nothing was filed. Ask Ines to top up practice dollars.
InsufficientBalance.why: The Teller Desk or AccountBlox refused because the ERC-20 amount exceeds free `balanceOf(account)`. For a wire, the desk checks before filing; a pending wire is a count, not escrowed funds, so the check prevents an already-unsettleable wire but cannot reserve funds against later spend-down. Ines can restore the demo balance up to the opening amount.

InvalidPayment.line: The payment details don't add up.

OperationFailed.line: The account tried, but the operation failed.

InvalidOperationType.line: This counter doesn't offer that service.
InvalidOperationType.why: The operation type hash is not registered in the account's function schemas.

ZeroOperationTypeNotAllowed.line: This counter doesn't offer that service.

NotSupported.line: This branch doesn't offer that yet.
NotSupported.why: The function is not supported by this account.

FunctionSelectorMismatch.line: That slip names a service this counter doesn't provide.
FunctionSelectorMismatch.why: The execution selector does not match the schema it was submitted under.

HandlerForSelectorMismatch.line: That slip names a service this counter doesn't provide.
HandlerForSelectorMismatch.why: The handler registered for this selector is not the one that was called.

ConflictingMetaTxPermissions.line: Those two permissions can't both be granted — the branch keeps them apart on purpose.
ConflictingMetaTxPermissions.why: The role registry refuses one role holding both the sign and the execute half of a meta-transaction action on one selector. It is why a priority release takes two desks: you sign (SIGN_META_APPROVE), the manager submits (EXECUTE_META_APPROVE).

InternalFunctionNotAccessible.line: That's an internal desk — customers can't call it.

ContractFunctionMustBeProtected.line: That function must stay behind the counter.
ContractFunctionMustBeProtected.why: Registry rule: contract functions must be protected.

DefinitionNotIDefinition.line: The branch's rule book is misconfigured — please tell the manager.
DefinitionNotIDefinition.why: A definitions library address is not an IDefinition contract.

OnlyCallableByContract.line: Only the account itself can do that.

InvalidAddress.line: That address isn't one the counter can take.

NotNewAddress.line: That's the same address as before.
NotNewAddress.why: The new value equals the current value.

TimeLockPeriodZero.line: A cooling period of zero isn't allowed here.

NewTimelockSame.why: New timelock equals the current one.

RoleWalletLimitReached.line: That list is full — take one off before adding another.
RoleWalletLimitReached.why: The role's `maxWallets` cap was reached, so `addWallet` reverted. The terminal's viewing list checks the cap first (`OBSERVER_FULL`) so the refusal costs no transaction.

MaxWalletsZero.line: A role needs room for at least one wallet.

MaxRolesExceeded.line: The branch has all the roles it can hold.

MaxHooksExceeded.line: Too many hooks on that function.

MaxFunctionsExceeded.line: That role covers as many services as it can.

ArrayLengthMismatch.line: The paperwork doesn't line up — let's redo it.

IndexOutOfBounds.line: The paperwork doesn't line up — let's redo it.

BatchSizeExceeded.line: Too much in one batch — the desk will split it.

RangeSizeExceeded.line: Too much in one batch — the desk will split it.

InvalidRange.line: The paperwork doesn't line up — let's redo it.

InvalidOperation.line: That's not an operation this counter can do.

CustomError.line: The account said no, and it said why in its own words.
CustomError.why: A custom error the SDK could not name. Raw data is in the message.

ReadableText.why: A string revert. On Remote EVM an empty revert after idle time usually means an expired meta-transaction — see REMOTE-EVM.md §1a.

Unknown.line: The vault would not accept that.
Unknown.why: The revert data could not be decoded — often a Sepolia RPC flake during pre-flight simulation, or a nested error with no custom-error selector. Retry Release; if it persists, check owner ETH and desk logs for the cause chain.

OwnerGasDry.line: Your wallet needs a little more ETH for gas — ask Ines to re-check your account.
OwnerGasDry.why: Lane B wire/release is paid by the owner's embedded wallet. Below a tiny floor, viem simulation often fails as an opaque Unknown instead of a clear insufficient-funds revert. Re-check tops up to SEPOLIA_OWNER_GAS_ETH / OWNER_GAS_ETH.

RpcError.line: The chain did not answer clearly — try Release again in a moment.
RpcError.why: HTTP/RPC/timeout or nonce-class failure while preparing or simulating the vault call. The record is unchanged; retrying is safe.

NO_ACCOUNT.line: You don't have an account here yet — Ines at Account Opening will sort you out.
NO_ACCOUNT.why: The Teller Desk has no AccountBlox on file for your wallet. Open one first.

NOT_CONFIGURED.line: Your account is on file, but the desks aren't authorised for it yet — ask Ines to re-check your account.
NOT_CONFIGURED.why: The Teller Desk knows your account address but never recorded the end of provisioning (`configured` / `roleSet`), so the role grants the counter and the vault need may be missing. Ines's "Re-check my account" runs the provisioner again: it reads the chain first and only sends what is missing.

FAUCET_OFF.line: Practice top-ups are available on the Main wing only.
FAUCET_OFF.why: The practice faucet hands over demo dollars from the branch's own till, so it works wherever that till exists: Sepolia on the live branch (where the practice token is open-mint and the till refills itself) and Remote EVM 1337 in Developer Mode. It never funds the deferred Arc wing, whose money is real native USDC.

FAUCET_EMPTY.line: The branch's practice treasury is short today — no top-up was sent.
FAUCET_EMPTY.why: The deployer treasury did not hold the exact delta needed to bring this account back to the configured opening balance. The faucet refuses instead of sending a partial or above-target amount.

FAUCET_TX_FAILED.line: The branch couldn't finish that practice top-up — no balance was promised.
FAUCET_TX_FAILED.why: The deployer transfer did not settle as expected, or the account's post-transfer balance was still below the configured opening amount.

NO_WALLET.line: Your sign-in has no wallet attached yet — try the desk again.
NO_WALLET.why: The Privy user has no embedded EVM wallet; the overlay creates one at Account Opening.

NO_MANAGER.line: The manager isn't in today — release it yourself at the vault window.
NO_MANAGER.why: The Teller Desk has no `MANAGER_PK`, so the BRANCH_MANAGER runtime role has no holder on this branch (T3 lore mode).

MANAGER_NO_STAMP.line: The manager doesn't stamp vault releases any more — Bob does, once the clock runs down.
MANAGER_NO_STAMP.why: U4+ removed `EXECUTE_TIME_DELAY_APPROVE` from BRANCH_MANAGER on the transfer selector, and `/approve` refuses `as: manager`. Okafor's desk is the priority bypass (your hand scan, his submit) and the shredder.

NOT_COOLING.line: That one's done cooling — Bob releases it at the vault window, no hand scan needed.
NOT_COOLING.why: A priority release is only for a record still before its `releaseTime`. Once the clock has run down the direct, time-checked `approveTimeLockExecution` is open to you (silent), and the manager does not stamp it: Okafor bypasses cooling, he is not a second Bob.

PRIORITY_OFF.line: This branch runs vault-only — nobody skips the cooling here.
PRIORITY_OFF.why: `PRIORITY_RELEASE` is off: accounts carry no META_APPROVE permissions on `transfer`, so the untimed meta-approve path has no permission-holder and the clock is the only way out (the U2 invariant).

PRIORITY_CANCELLED.line: No hand scan, no priority release — the wire keeps cooling.
PRIORITY_CANCELLED.why: The Privy sign sheet, or the Passkey prompt before it, was dismissed. Nothing was signed and nothing was sent; the record is still PENDING.

MFA_FAILED.line: The hand scan didn't take — try again when you're ready.
MFA_FAILED.why: Privy's second factor (Passkey) failed, timed out or hit its retry limit, so the bypass payload was never signed. `promptMfa()` asks every time; there is no cached scan to fall back on.

PRIORITY_EXPIRED.line: That priority slip has gone stale — let's start again.
PRIORITY_EXPIRED.why: The prepared meta-approve (deadline = block time + 10 min, drift-corrected) expired or was already used before the signature came back. Prepare a fresh one; the nonce moves on.

CONSOLE_UNAVAILABLE.line: The screen is dark — this branch terminal only runs in the bank shell.
CONSOLE_UNAVAILABLE.why: The terminal panel (an iframe of the hosted Console) belongs to the browser shell in apps/web. Off the web build, or under MockChain, there is no panel to open — the viewing-wallet verbs still work, the window does not.

OBSERVER_SELF.line: That wallet already has a place on this account — it doesn't need a viewing pass.
OBSERVER_SELF.why: The address is the account holder, the teller's broadcaster, the branch manager, or the account itself. Each already holds a role, so `_validateAnyRole()` already lets it read; adding it to OBSERVER would grant nothing and would put a bank key on your viewing list.

OBSERVER_FULL.line: Your viewing list is full — take one off before adding another.
OBSERVER_FULL.why: The OBSERVER role is created with a `maxWallets` cap; the protocol enforces it as `RoleWalletLimitReached`. The desk checks first so the refusal costs no transaction.

NOT_OBSERVER.line: That address isn't on your viewing list.
NOT_OBSERVER.why: `REVOKE_WALLET` was asked for an address the OBSERVER role does not hold (or the role was never created on this account). Nothing was sent.

ACCOUNT_NOT_OWNED.line: That account isn't yours — the ledger names somebody else as its holder, so I can't put it on your file.
ACCOUNT_NOT_OWNED.why: Load Account reads `owner()` on the address and compares it to the wallet you signed in with. They differ, so the desk refused before anything was written or signed. This is the whole safety of loading by number: an account number is public, and knowing one must never be enough to have the branch treat that account as yours. Ownership can only be moved by the account itself, through Security's recovery desk.

ACCOUNT_NOT_A_VAULT.line: There's no account of ours at that number on this wing — check the number, and check you're at the right branch.
ACCOUNT_NOT_A_VAULT.why: The address has no contract on this chain (a plain wallet address, or an account number from the other wing — Live and Developer Mode are different chains and their accounts cannot be swapped), or it has a contract that is not an initialised AccountBlox: the desk requires `owner()` to answer, `initialized()` to be true and ERC-165 `ISecureOwnable` to be supported. Measured on the lab chain: the demo token has code but reverts on `owner()`, and CopyBlox itself answers `IBaseStateMachine` while failing both of the others — which is why the factory cannot be loaded as an account.

LOAD_POLICY.line: I couldn't move your signing rules over to that account, so I've left your file as it was.
LOAD_POLICY.why: Loading an account re-points the Privy policy rules (typed data for the Bloxchain domain, and the owner's own vault transactions) at the new address *before* the player index is changed. Privy refused that update, so the load was abandoned rather than completed: the alternative is a desk that files account B while the enclave will only ever sign for account A. Nothing on the chain was touched.

INVALID_NAME.line: Petra needs one valid label under branchzero.eth.
INVALID_NAME.why: ENSIP-15 normalization or the Name Desk's one-label boundary rejected the input. Customer claims cannot smuggle another hierarchy into the branch.

NAME_TAKEN.line: That name is already on the board — try another.
NAME_TAKEN.why: The customers UserRegistry reports this label as REGISTERED, so the registrar will not mint it a second time.

NAME_NOT_FOUND.line: There is no customer name like that on the board.
NAME_NOT_FOUND.why: The pinned ENSv2 Universal Resolver returned no addr(60) record for this branchzero.eth name.

NAME_NOT_OWNED.line: That name does not point to your account.
NAME_NOT_OWNED.why: The Name Desk will only edit a text record after resolving the name and checking that it points to this player's AccountBlox.

ENS_NOT_CONFIGURED.line: Petra's Sepolia register is not configured today.
ENS_NOT_CONFIGURED.why: The Name Desk needs the pinned ENSv2 deployment, SEPOLIA_RPC_URL and the env-only ENS_REGISTRAR_PK. No Remote EVM key can be used here.

ENS_RPC.line: Petra can't reach the Sepolia name register right now.
ENS_RPC.why: The ENSv2 read failed at the Sepolia RPC boundary. Nothing was paid: the name never resolved, so no payment was attempted on either wing.

ENS_TX_FAILED.line: The Sepolia name register refused that record.
ENS_TX_FAILED.why: The registrar or resolver transaction did not mine successfully. The Name Desk does not pretend a failed transaction was claimed.

ENS_RECORD_FAILED.line: The name was registered, but its account pointer needs Petra's attention.
ENS_RECORD_FAILED.why: After the resolver write, the pinned Universal Resolver did not return the player's AccountBlox. No payment was attempted.

AUTH.line: I'll need you signed in for that — Ines can help at Account Opening.
AUTH.why: The Teller Desk rejected the request: no Privy access token, or the wallet address does not belong to the authenticated user.

LOGIN_CANCELLED.line: No rush — come back when you're ready to sign in.
LOGIN_CANCELLED.why: The Privy sign-in was dismissed before completing.

POLICY.line: That's above what I can do at this counter — it goes through the vault.
POLICY.why: Branch policy: amounts over the instant limit are routed to the time-locked lane. This limit is enforced by the Teller Desk, not by the contract (REFLECTION §2.2 partial invariant).

BAD_ARGS.line: I can't read that slip — check the payee and the amount.
BAD_ARGS.why: The bridge or the Teller Desk rejected the arguments (not an address, not a decimal amount, not a record id).

TIMEOUT.line: The desk is taking longer than usual — the board will catch up when it answers.
TIMEOUT.why: No response from the bridge within the call's timeout. The Teller Desk may still complete the job; stage events and the focus reconcile will update the board.

RPC.line: The branch can't reach the ledger right now.
RPC.why: Network or HTTP failure between the shell and the Teller Desk / RPC.

CHAIN.line: The ledger isn't answering — try again in a moment.
CHAIN.why: Chain-level failure reported by the bridge.

UNKNOWN_METHOD.why: The game asked the bridge for a method it does not expose. Add a bridge method that calls an existing Teller Desk route (HANDOFF §5c).

NOT_IMPLEMENTED.line: That desk opens in a later unit.
NOT_IMPLEMENTED.why: Route exists but is planned for a later construction unit (ENS U5, FX S1).

INTERNAL.line: Something went wrong behind the counter.
INTERNAL.why: Unclassified failure in the bridge or the Teller Desk. The message is below.

FX_NOT_CONFIGURED.line: The FX board is dark today — the branch can't reach the exchange floor.
FX_NOT_CONFIGURED.why: The Teller Desk has no Sepolia RPC, no FX teller key, or no Uniswap v4 pool pinned in infra/deployments/sepolia.json. The desk closes the board rather than quote a price it cannot honour; Counter and the vault run on another chain and are unaffected.

FX_TILL_CLOSED.line: You've no till on the exchange floor yet — Kenji can open one.
FX_TILL_CLOSED.why: The FX desk trades from an AccountBlox of yours on Sepolia — the same one Ines opened if you are on the live branch, a separate till in Developer Mode. None exists for your owner address yet, and the branch has no funded deployer there to clone one.

FX_NOT_ENABLED.line: The exchange door isn't on your approved list yet — Kenji registers it first.
FX_NOT_ENABLED.why: GuardController has no schema or whitelist entry for the router's execute selector on this account, so the call would be refused. Registering the three functions and their three targets is one owner-signed guard batch.

FX_TELLER_DRY.line: The FX teller is out of gas money — the desk can't submit trades today.
FX_TELLER_DRY.why: The Sepolia broadcaster that pays for your swap meta-transactions holds too little ETH to cover one guarded call. It never holds your funds; it only pays gas.

FX_TILL_SHORT.line: Your FX till hasn't the dollars for that order.
FX_TILL_SHORT.why: The swap spends practice dollars held by your Sepolia till. On the live branch that till *is* the account Ines opened, so her faucet tops it up; in Developer Mode your Main account is on the lab chain and the till is a separate Sepolia account her faucet cannot reach. Nothing was signed; the order was refused before any approval.

FX_AMOUNT.line: That is not an amount the dealer can price.
FX_AMOUNT.why: A quote takes a positive decimal amount of the input token, in display units.

FX_QUOTE_FAILED.line: The exchange wouldn't price that — try a smaller amount.
FX_QUOTE_FAILED.why: The v4 Quoter reverted for this size: the pool is thin, or the amount is more than one hop can fill. Quoting is an eth_call, so nothing was signed or spent.

FX_QUOTE_EXPIRED.line: That quote has gone stale — let me price it again.
FX_QUOTE_EXPIRED.why: Quotes carry a five-minute deadline and are held against your name until then. Rather than silently re-price a trade you agreed at another rate, the desk refuses and asks for a fresh quote.

FX_SLIPPAGE.line: The rate moved past your floor — nothing was traded.
FX_SLIPPAGE.why: The router refused because the pool would return less than the minimum the quote fixed (the quote minus your slippage). The trade reverts whole and the money stays in the till.

FX_ROUTER.line: The exchange refused that trade — nothing left your till.
FX_ROUTER.why: The Universal Router reverted during the desk's pre-flight, so no meta-transaction was signed or submitted. Usual causes: an expired deadline, a pool with no liquidity at that size, or a malformed route.

FX_RPC.line: Kenji can't reach the exchange floor right now.
FX_RPC.why: A Sepolia read failed. The FX desk is a side path: the Main-wing counter, vault and ledger board are on another chain and keep working.

FX_TX_FAILED.line: That trade was mined but did not complete — nothing was swapped.
FX_TX_FAILED.why: The transaction reached the chain and reverted, or ran out of the gas its record reserved. Balances are unchanged; only the teller's gas was spent.

FX_TILL_NOT_SEPOLIA.line: That account isn't on the exchange floor — the FX desk only trades on Sepolia.
FX_TILL_NOT_SEPOLIA.why: The FX desk trades through an AccountBlox that really exists on Sepolia and is really owned by you. The address offered had no contract there, or belongs to someone else — which is exactly what a Main-wing account from another chain looks like on Sepolia. The desk checks with one read before signing anything.

FX_SEPOLIA_ONLY.line: Currency exchange happens on Sepolia only — that's where the pool is.
FX_SEPOLIA_ONLY.why: Uniswap v4 is deployed on public testnets, not on the branch's private development chain. So FX writes are always Sepolia, in Live and in Developer Mode alike, and they need a real Sepolia account of yours. Payments and the vault use whichever wing you are in.

FX_PAIR.line: The desk deals in euros and shekels only — not that.
FX_PAIR.why: Kenji sells practice dollars for Practice EUR or Practice ILS, one-way, through two Uniswap v4 pools. Any other currency — ether included since the fiat pairs of 2026-09-09 — has no pool behind this counter, so the desk refuses before anything is priced or signed.

DEV_DESK_DOWN.line: The development branch isn't answering — the live branch is still open.
DEV_DESK_DOWN.why: Developer Mode talks to a second Teller Desk on the private lab chain (Remote EVM 1337). It is an operator convenience and is never published; if it is not running, Live is the branch to use.
